title: Prompt–Response Harmony: pacing-driven continuous scheduler with KV compaction
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Goal: implement a pacing-driven continuous batching scheduler that balances prompt and response length skew while limiting KV cache fragmentation and GPU memory pressure.

Context: Our current continuous batcher groups streams primarily by arrival time and sequence length bins which yields suboptimal behavior with mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts with long generated tails and vice versa). This causes: 1) unpredictable tail latency for latency-sensitive requests, 2) KV cache fragmentation across GPU slabs, and 3) oscillating GPU memory utilization during bursty dialogues.

Approach summary: introduce per-request soft deadlines (pacing budgets) derived from client-level SLO and token budget, use those budgets to prioritize micro-batch inclusion and preemption; coordinate with a lightweight KV compaction/fragmentation controller that performs opportunistic delta-encoding and hot-key pinning to reduce occupied KV slab footprint. Key ideas: pacing windows (ms budgets), urgency score = f(remaining_tokens, client_slo, observed_service_time), micro-batch admission that respects urgency and memory headroom, lazy KV materialization for speculative prefixes, and a background compaction pass that coalesces small KV segments during low GPU utilization.

Deliverables: scheduler plugin implementing pacing windows + urgency queue, KV compaction controller (C++ runtime component + Python control API), integration tests and perf harness, benchmark results vs baseline (continuous-batcher-1.18) showing 95th percentile latency improvement for mixed workloads and <=5% steady-state throughput loss, rollout plan with canary + fallback to existing scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler respects per-request pacing budgets: less than 10% violations for requests with explicit latency SLO in synthetic benchmarks
KV compaction reduces median KV slab occupancy by >= 18% on mixed prompt/response traces without increasing cold-miss rates by >5%
95th percentile latency for a mixed-length dialog benchmark improves by >= 12% compared to baseline continuous-batcher
End-to-end regression tests added and green in CI; perf dashboard shows no regressions on stable workloads
Canary rollout automation and automatic fallback to legacy scheduler implemented
steps: Design doc: define pacing budget formula, urgency score, memory headroom heuristics, compaction window
Prototype scheduler in Python harness to iterate on admission heuristics using production traces
Implement scheduler plugin in C++ runtime with bounded priority queue and micro-batch preemption hooks
Implement KV compaction controller: delta-encoding, segment coalescing, hot-key pinning interfaces
Add telemetry: per-request pacing decisions, KV segment map, GPU slab utilization, preemption counts
Benchmark: run mixed-length traces (customer and synthetic), compare against baseline on dedicated GPU pool
Code review and iterate; add end-to-end tests and CI perf checks
Rollout: canary on 5% traffic with observability gates; fallback automation if SLO regressions occur
